question: Nitin starts from Point Y and drives 13 km towards south. He then takes a right turn, drives 59 km, turns left and drives 49 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 21 km. He takes a left turn, drives 37 km. He then turns right, drives 38 km, turns right and drives 23 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution:
Given:

Nitin starts from Point Y and drives 13 km towards south.

Then, he takes a right turn and drives 59 km.

Next, he turns left and drives 49 km, then takes a left turn and drives 21 km.

He takes a left turn and drives 37 km, then turns right and drives 38 km.

Finally, he turns right and drives 23 km to stop at Point Z.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f58c421be78a06f2e0dd88347599e76a6cce406f8581e38191be0d66bf7d96c3.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a82f66d3794cbdf3806a105acbc8f743b08fa59b6e21445a916bad08854c0d56.png] 

So, Point Z is 48 km South from his starting point Y. To reach Point Y again, he must drive 48 km towards North.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**
